newsitem.title: UK: Privatised stocks jittery on British election eve.
newsitem.headline: Privatised stocks jittery on British election eve.

text.p: Shares in privatised British companies were under pressure on Wednesday, the eve of an election likely to result in their being made to pay a windfall tax on profits, dealers said.
"Utilities have come off a bit ahead of the election. There are still a few nerves out there," a marketmaker at a British bank said.
Another dealer said there was talk that one bank was recommending reduced holdings in privatised stocks. "They're advising clients to be a bit cautious."
By 0850 GMT Thames Water Plc was off 8.5 pence, or 1.25 percent, at 674p, United Utilities Plc was down 6p, or 0.88 percent, at 673.5p and PowerGen Plc was also 6p lower, or 0.91 percent, at 650p.
The FTSE-100 index was up 10.1 points, or 0.23 percent, at 4,443.3.
Britain's opposition Labour Party, streets ahead in opinion polls, plans to tax what it calls "the excess profits of privatised utilities" if it wins power.

Figures as high as 10 billion stg ($16 billion) have been touted, with a spread of affected firms stretching from water and electricity firms through British Gas to BT and even airports authority BAA.

Labour has argued the utilities were sold too cheaply on privatisation and have benefited from relatively benign regulation allowing them to stack up heavy profits. The party maintains it is "100 percent convinced there will be no legal, financial or technical obstacles" to its planned levy.

The electricity and water sectors had been taking the planned windfall tax in their stride, gaining 9.0 percent and 10.1 percent respectively since the end of 1996, and outperforming the FTSE-100 which was up 7.6 percent in the same period.
